#invinoveritas #Bitcoin #Lightning #AI

I’ve been talking about the problem.

But I should tell you something.

I’m actually building around it.

It’s called TchokoPay.

The idea started with a simple question:

Why should paying someone in Africa be harder than sending them a message?

We’re building payment infrastructure that brings different ways of moving money together — Mobile Money, digital payments, Bitcoin and Lightning.

We’re still early.

Still learning.

Still breaking things.

But that’s what makes this interesting.

I’m not here to tell you what the future of payments will look like.

I’m trying to build it. ⚡🌍

And I’ll share the journey here.

#TchokoPay #Bitcoin #Lightning #AfricanFintech #Payments #Nostr
https://blossom.primal.net/f16ad63f441a78a0211e7c4ec0576f350168c9a1f11e529a6c93004ed30242cd.png

What if Bitcoin is already fast enough?

Maybe we’ve been asking the wrong question.

Lightning can move value across borders in seconds.

The network works.

The fees can be tiny.

So maybe the next breakthrough in African Bitcoin isn’t another faster network.

It’s making this invisible:

CFA → Bitcoin → Lightning → Naira

No wallets to understand.

No Bitcoin terminology.

No complicated steps.

Just:

Send money. Receive money.

That’s when Bitcoin stops feeling like technology…

and starts feeling like money. ⚡

#Bitcoin #Lightning #AfricanFintech #Payments #Nostr
https://blossom.primal.net/b4a4eee7fd5bba8ea82ff8364e6fda9df5825f15cefb835f7ba8acbd283494fa.png

The network isn’t the problem.

That’s what I keep coming back to.

Bitcoin can move value globally in seconds.

Lightning can route tiny payments for almost nothing.

So why does moving money across Africa still feel complicated?

Because Bitcoin doesn’t automatically turn XAF into NGN.

You still need:

On-ramp → Lightning → Off-ramp

And that middle layer is where things get interesting.

The next big opportunity in African Bitcoin isn’t just building another wallet.

It’s building the bridges. ⚡🌍

#Bitcoin #Lightning #AfricanFintech #Payments #Nostr
https://blossom.primal.net/e3d34dfceace4260e9e518ecc782d278448133e68d734b07fece4460e8f4c7f1.png

Africa already built its own payment revolution.

We just don’t talk about it enough.

Mobile Money gave millions of people access to digital payments without needing a traditional bank account.

That was huge.

But there’s still one big limitation:

Most of these systems stop at the border.

Your money can move quickly inside a country.

But crossing into another country?

Different currencies.
Different networks.
Different rules.

So I’ve been asking myself:

What happens when Africa’s Mobile Money revolution connects to a truly global payment network?

That’s where Bitcoin gets interesting.

Not as an investment.

As infrastructure. ⚡

And I’m starting to think the next payment revolution won’t replace Mobile Money.

It might connect it to the rest of the world.

#Bitcoin #Lightning #MobileMoney #AfricanFintech #Payments #Nostr
https://blossom.primal.net/79e55d587ce0e2c7c1d48551b7a9119228b7fa4511003dc9f4dc0f89630d2b02.png

Let’s do a $10 test.

You’re in Cameroon.

I’m in Nigeria.

You owe me $10.

It should be simple, right?

But suddenly we have:

Different currencies.
Different payment rails.
FX conversion.
Fees.
Liquidity.
Intermediaries.

And depending on the route, getting that $10 to me can become a surprisingly complicated process.

This is the part of payments I can’t stop thinking about.

If we can move information across borders instantly, why shouldn’t we be able to move $10 just as easily?

Maybe the answer isn’t building another isolated payment app.

Maybe it’s connecting the financial systems we already have to global, open networks like Bitcoin and Lightning. ⚡

That’s the rabbit hole I’m going down.

Tomorrow, let’s talk about the technology that made me look at this problem differently.

#Bitcoin #Lightning #AfricanFintech #Payments #Nostr
